Adriana, you missed the meeting, so here is what happened. The finance director said the budget had already been approved, which was news to everybody in the room. Then the head of operations said he could not release his people in March, and he asked whether we had considered starting in April instead. Nobody answered that. The vice president said he wanted one owner for the initiative, not three, and he told me to send you the list of action items today. There is one thing I would not put in the minutes: after the call, the operations director told me, off the record, that he had already decided to leave the company. So think carefully about who you make the owner.

Hello, this is Peter from the regional office. I am escalating something and I want it on record. Three weeks ago the site manager told my team that the training had been completed. Last week he said it was almost finished. Yesterday he said he had never received the material. Those three statements cannot all be true, and I am not interested in which one is a lie. What I want is a debrief with the three of us in the room, this week, and I want the minutes written by somebody who was not involved. I have asked the compliance officer whether she can take them. If she cannot, tell me who can, and we will move on.
